glyph_origin: According to the Shuowen Jiezi, a pictogram (象形) of a baby without arms. Compare with 子, where the arms are visible. The Shuowen defines 了 as "the crossing of lower legs". In the Shuowen Jiezi Zhu, a commentary to the Shuowen Jiezi, it is said that the pictogram instead depicts entangled legs (了戾). Its relation with the meaning "to finish" is likely via sound loan, but an argument can be made about "entangled legs" → "tie"→ "finish". Unrelated to 亨.
shuowen: According to the Shuowen Jiezi, a pictogram (象形) of a baby without arms.
The Shuowen defines 了 as "the crossing of lower legs".
senses: [le] Used after a verb to indicate perfective aspect (action completion).
[le] Used at the end of a sentence to indicate a change of state.
[liǎo] to be finished; to be completed
